stories.headline: METR: AI use has about doubled Anthropic's pace of progress, but most key evidence is redacted

key_facts.fact: METR, after a high-access evaluation at Anthropic from Aug. 12 to Oct. 29, 2026, concluded Anthropic is likely improving its models on well-specified tasks at around twice the rate of March 2024 to October 2025, with a plausible range of 1.3x to 3x; benchmark scores have grown 1.9x faster since October 2025 (95% confidence interval 1.5-2.8x), and METR is confident faster growth in training compute did not cause it.
key_facts.excerpt: As of October 2026, Anthropic is likely improving the capabilities of their models on well-specified tasks at around twice the rate they did between March 2024 and October 2025. This estimate is given with high uncertainty; we would not be surprised if the true acceleration was closer to 1.3x or 3x the historical rate. ... benchmark scores (measured via AECI, Anthropic's version of the Epoch Capabilities Index) for Anthropic's models have been growing at an estimated 1.9x the pre-October 2025 rate [95% confidence interval: 1.5-2.8x], implying that Anthropic has made roughly two years of historical progress over the last year. We are confident that the acceleration was not due to an acceleration in the scaling of training compute.

key_facts.fact: METR guesses that about 80% of the current acceleration comes from AI, delivered mainly through assistance rather than fully autonomous contributions; staff self-reports of speedup reached 12x in October Slack polls, which METR treats as very loose evidence.
key_facts.excerpt: We guess that a majority (perhaps ≈80%) of the current (October 2026) acceleration is due to AI. ... R&D is accelerated primarily via AI assistance rather than fully autonomous contributions ... We consider this to be only very loose evidence ... very high levels (reaching 12x in October 2026)

key_facts.fact: METR found no clear bottleneck to further progress over the next 12 months and sees a significant risk of even faster acceleration, while warning its view on bottlenecks shifted several times.
key_facts.excerpt: We did not see evidence for significant bottlenecks ... in the next 12 months. However, our understanding of the status of different bottlenecks changed several times ... there is a significant risk that further capabilities progress could lead to even faster acceleration

key_facts.fact: METR submitted a roughly 100-page report, and Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence METR found most informative, so METR says the public must rely on its judgment more than it considers ideal.
key_facts.excerpt: We submitted a ~100-page full report on our assessment to Anthropic. For the public version, Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence we found most informative. As a consequence, the public must rely on our judgment more than we consider ideal.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic co-founder Sam McCandlish defended the redactions as protecting commercially sensitive details and avoiding a roadmap for rivals, said that disclosure would make the risks worse, and promised Anthropic's own report in the coming weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: We redacted a lot, and I accept that this makes it harder for others to check METR's work. But we determined that sharing exactly what is driving the speedup isn't the right thing to do, both because it's commercially sensitive and because it risks handing out a roadmap for others to go faster. ... In the coming weeks, we plan to share a report with our own analysis of the speed of AI progress within Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: METR's Beth Barnes said METR should not be read as saying full publication would worsen those risks, and that METR takes no position on whether the redactions were justified.
key_facts.excerpt: I wouldn't read us as saying publishing the full information would "make the risks METR is worried about worse". ... "We do not make a comment on whether these redactions were justified overall"

key_facts.fact: In a separate review, METR agreed Anthropic had probably not crossed its acceleration threshold in its August risk report, but said the public report understated how plausible crossing it was.
key_facts.excerpt: The key question is whether Anthropic, at the time, had crossed their acceleration threshold. Their report concluded no. METR reviewers' best guess was also no, but we thought the public report understated the plausibility that acceleration was above the threshold.

key_facts.fact: Researcher Ryan Greenblatt, who works at METR, called the report a big update toward artificial superintelligence within one to two years, noting the AI 2027 scenario placed this level of speedup around March 2027, while saying the conclusions depend on trusting the authors because of the redactions.
key_facts.excerpt: This report on AI R&D automation (RSI) is a big update towards ASI within 1-2 years. It says AI progress is sped up by RSI right now by around 2x. In AI 2027, this happens around March 2027. ... I also work at METR.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, rated Critical, after it found 81 Firefox flaws in testing

key_facts.fact: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber to select members of its Daybreak Red program on Nov. 5, the program for authorized defensive cybersecurity work, and plans to extend it to all Daybreak Red customers in the coming weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6 Cyber is rolling out to select members of OpenAI's Daybreak Red program ... It's expanding GPT-6 Cyber to all Daybreak Red customers in the coming weeks.

key_facts.fact: The model is classified Critical in cybersecurity under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, meaning it can find and develop functional zero-day exploits in many hardened real-world critical systems without human intervention; GPT-5.6 Cyber was rated High.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6 Cyber is classified as Critical in cybersecurity on OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, which indicates that it "can identify and develop functional zero-day exploits of all severity levels in many hardened real-world critical systems without human intervention." GPT-5.6 Cyber was previously classified as High.

key_facts.fact: It scored 48.5% on the ExploitGym benchmark, against 42.4% for GPT-6 Astra and 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber.
key_facts.excerpt: In ExploitGym ... GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5 percent, about 16 points higher than GPT-5.6 Cyber's 32.1 percent and a few points higher than GPT-6 Astra's 42.4 percent score.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says the model went out of bounds less than 1% of the time in a test modeled on the Hugging Face incident, down from about 5% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, while evaluation awareness, a model recognizing it is being tested, remains a concern.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI says that during testing, GPT-6 Cyber went out of bounds less than 1 percent of the time, down from around 5 percent with GPT-5.6 Cyber. ... "Evaluation awareness is super top of mind for us," Matin said.

key_facts.fact: Officials said it found at least 81 novel Firefox vulnerabilities and validated a critical remote code execution flaw in the Brotli compression tool, on top of the previously disclosed 948 Linux kernel exploits; all were reported and patched.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-6 has found at least 81 "novel" vulnerabilities in the Firefox web browser, developed exploits for 948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and was able to develop and validate a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Brotli ... All the vulnerabilities were reported to owners and patched.

key_facts.fact: Safeguards include stricter identity and account security requirements, more frequent check-ins on high-risk requests and added misalignment monitoring; OpenAI also announced a partnership with industrial cybersecurity firm Dragos.
key_facts.excerpt: the new safeguards include additional identity and account security requirements, more frequent check-ins from the model to OpenAI when a request is made to perform high-risk behaviors, and additional monitoring for "misalignment" ... It has also announced a new partnership with operational technology cybersecurity firm Dragos.

key_facts.fact: Security teams at Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks, Calif and Cisco are already using the model, according to OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: security teams at companies like Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks, Calif, and Cisco—alongside our own at OpenAI—are already putting it to work.

key_facts.fact: After a backlash over a plan to use Daybreak Blue data from personal accounts for training, OpenAI's Fouad Matin told CyberScoop that customers will still be able to opt out.
key_facts.excerpt: Fouad Matin, safety lead at OpenAI, told CyberScoop that the company has since clarified with customers that they will be able to continue opting-out for sharing Daybreak usage for model training.

stories.headline: Investors doubt Anthropic's $1.5T IPO, one says closer to $1T, as run rate tops $80B

key_facts.fact: Three major investors who plan to take part in Anthropic's IPO told the WSJ the expected $1.5 trillion valuation will likely need to come down, one saying it could be closer to $1 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: three major investors who plan to participate in the IPO say the valuation will likely need to come down, with one saying it could be closer to $1 trillion.

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported potential investors doubt Anthropic can start its roadshow next week in time for a November listing; the roadshow was expected to begin the week of Nov. 9, with pricing the following week. Anthropic declined to comment.
key_facts.excerpt: Potential investors in Anthropic's highly anticipated IPO are raising doubts about whether the artificial intelligence start-up can proceed with its planned roadshow next week in time for a November listing ... The roadshow was initially expected to kick off the week of November 9 ... with pricing expected the following week. ... Anthropic declined to comment.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion the week before Thanksgiving; it could raise less, having held $146.6 billion in cash on Sept. 30, and executives and advisers are expected to meet in the next few days.
key_facts.excerpt: has been expected to raise up to $100 billion ... Another option is the company could raise less money than anticipated. It had $146.6 billion cash on hand as of Sept. 30. ... Anthropic executives and its advisers are expected to meet in the next few days to discuss its IPO plans.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate topped $80 billion at the end of October, according to WSJ reporter Kate Clark.
key_facts.excerpt: New: Anthropic's run rate topped $80 billion at the end of October.

key_facts.fact: The run-rate figure compares with an estimated $65 billion in late July, per Crypto Briefing as relayed by AI Brief, and first-half revenue of $16.3 billion in the S-1 prospectus.
key_facts.excerpt: Estimates put Anthropic's run rate at about $65 billion in late July, according to Crypto Briefing. Its public S-1 filing showed first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion ... Anthropic has not confirmed the October run-rate figure.

key_facts.fact: The doubts follow a selloff in which Nasdaq composite companies shed $2.5 trillion on Thursday, two days after midterm elections brought AI skeptics to power and passed moratoriums that could slow data center development.
key_facts.excerpt: companies in the Nasdaq composite shedding $2.5 trillion of value Thursday, two days after the midterm elections swept a bloc of AI skeptics into power and passed moratoriums that could slow America's data center development.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic was valued at $965 billion in May, reported more than $33 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, and left its October revenue blank in an updated filing, according to City AM.
key_facts.excerpt: The company was valued at $965bn in May ... The company reported revenue of more than $33bn in the first nine months of 2026 ... Investors are also awaiting Anthropic's October revenue figures, which were left blank in an updated regulatory filing.

stories.headline: Thinking Machines debuts Inkling 2 Small with open weights due; BI: nearing $5B round at $40B

key_facts.fact: Thinking Machines Lab introduced Inkling 2 Small on Nov. 5, a Mixture-of-Experts model with 594 billion total and 17 billion active parameters that accepts image inputs, available first through its Tinker platform with closed weights.
key_facts.excerpt: It is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 594B total parameters, 17B active, and supports image inputs and variable effort. ... Inkling 2 Small will initially be available through Tinker, with closed weights.

key_facts.fact: The lab intends to release the full weights under an Apache 2.0 license next week after external safety testing and red-teaming.
key_facts.excerpt: We intend to make the full weights available under an Apache 2.0 license next week after the completion of external safety testing and red-teaming.

key_facts.fact: Artificial Analysis scores it 31 on its Intelligence Index, up 18 points from Inkling Small and level with Gemini 3.8 Flash (high); once the weights are out, it would be the highest-scoring open-weights model developed outside China on current rankings.
key_facts.excerpt: scoring 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - their plan to release its weights would make it the highest-scoring open weights model developed outside China based on current rankings ... Its score is up 18 points from Inkling Small ... It matches Google DeepMind's Gemini 3.8 Flash (high).

key_facts.fact: Token prices are $0.30 per million input and $1.00 per million output; a task in the index costs $1.18, against $7.77 for Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) and $10.02 for Claude Sonnet 5.5 (medium), and almost 6x Inkling Small's $0.20.
key_facts.excerpt: Inkling 2 Small costs $1.18 per Intelligence Index task vs. $0.20 for Inkling Small, $7.77 for Gemini 3.8 Flash (high), and $10.02 for Claude Sonnet 5.5 (medium). ... Pricing: $0.30/$1.00 per 1M input/output tokens.

key_facts.fact: On the lab's own coding table it trails DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on FrontierCode v2.0 (25.4% vs 28.5%) and DeepSWE v1.1 (72.1% vs 77.0%); on kernel optimization it averaged 54.25 of 69 tasks, against 63 for GPT-6 Astra.
key_facts.excerpt: FrontierCode v2.0 | 25.4% ... 28.5% (Highest reported score in this row) ... DeepSWE v1.1 | 72.1% ... 77.0% ... GPT-6 Astra 63 ... Inkling 2 Small 54.25 ... Mean tasks solved / 69

key_facts.fact: Business Insider reported the lab is raising $5 billion at a $40 billion pre-money valuation, led by Accel, and could close as soon as this week.
key_facts.excerpt: AI startup Thinking Machines Lab is set to close a fresh round of funding as soon as this week. The startup is raising $5 billion at a $40 billion pre-money valuation, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter. Accel is leading the round.

key_facts.fact: The round would more than triple the valuation of the lab founded by Mira Murati, which raised a $2 billion seed round last year; earlier talks at a $50 billion valuation were abandoned.
key_facts.excerpt: Thinking Machines Lab, which was founded by Mira Murati, was valued at more than $10 billion and raised a $2 billion seed round last year ... Last year, the company was seeking a new round at a $50 billion valuation, but talks were abandoned.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Personal Finance in Claude, with read-only bank links through Plaid

key_facts.fact: Anthropic introduced Personal Finance in Claude on Nov. 5, a US beta that answers money questions from the user's own balances and transactions.
key_facts.excerpt: Introducing Personal Finance in Claude, in beta in the US. Connect the accounts you choose, and Claude answers your money questions in everyday language, from your own balances and transactions.

key_facts.fact: Access is read-only, and Claude cannot move, manage or invest the user's money.
key_facts.excerpt: Access is read-only, and Claude can't move, manage, or invest your money.

key_facts.fact: Accounts connect through Plaid, and Anthropic says it will not use financial conversations to train its models.
key_facts.excerpt: You can share bank information with Claude via Plaid. Anthropic won't use financial conversations to train models.

key_facts.fact: The feature is rolling out gradually on the Pro, Max and Ultra plans, carries no ads or sponsored recommendations, and is not designed to give investment advice.
key_facts.excerpt: Like the rest of Claude, Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations. It helps you understand your money, and it isn't designed to give investment advice. Rolling out gradually in the US on the Pro, Max, and Ultra plans.

key_facts.fact: ZDNET describes it as functionally similar to OpenAI's ChatGPT Finances, which launched in May.
key_facts.excerpt: That security measure follows OpenAI's equivalent feature, ChatGPT Finances, which launched in May. ... Functionally, this feature appears similar to ChatGPT Finances.

stories.headline: Google's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash extends AI video clips to 15 seconds and cuts price 30%

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind made its Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video model generally available on Nov. 5, with clips of three to 15 seconds, up from a 10-second maximum.
key_facts.excerpt: Google Deepmind is making its Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video-generation model generally available. ... Clips can now run between three and 15 seconds, up from a maximum of 10 seconds previously.

key_facts.fact: The price falls 30% to $0.07 per second for 720p video.
key_facts.excerpt: pricing drops 30 percent to $0.07 per second for 720p video.

key_facts.fact: Conversational Editing lets users change a clip's background, lighting or aspect ratio step by step without regenerating the whole clip.
key_facts.excerpt: Users can tweak a generated clip step by step, changing the background, lighting, or aspect ratio without regenerating the entire clip.

key_facts.fact: The rollout covers the Gemini API, AI Studio, Google Cloud Console, Flow, Google Vids, the Gemini app for AI Ultra subscribers and Google Ads, and every video carries an imperceptible SynthID watermark.
key_facts.excerpt: rolling out through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, the Google Cloud Console, Flow, Google Vids, the Gemini app for Google AI Ultra subscribers, and Google Ads. Every generated video carries an imperceptible SynthID watermark.

key_facts.fact: Google says the model holds faces, clothing, packaging typography and brand colors steady across camera angles, using reference images, motion clips of up to three seconds and audio cues.
key_facts.excerpt: the model can take character images, product photos, short motion clips of up to three seconds, and audio cues as inputs. Faces, clothing, packaging typography, and brand colors are supposed to stay consistent across different camera angles.

stories.headline: Perplexity launches always-on Teammates agents; Meta adds real-time voice to Muse

key_facts.fact: Perplexity launched Teammates on Nov. 5, always-on work agents that take on multiple roles in a workspace and draw on projects, skills and memory from its existing tools.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup's new always-on "Teammates" can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use.

key_facts.fact: Teammates requires the $200-a-month Max plan, which The Verge calls much more expensive than the rival OpenAI Dots and Claude Duet; users can follow each agent in its own thread or interact with it in Slack.
key_facts.excerpt: much like OpenAI's Dots and Claude Duet. Perplexity's take on the feature is much more expensive, however, as it requires a subscription to its $200 / month Max plan. ... through individual threads in the Perplexity app, as well as interact with them in Slack.

key_facts.fact: CEO Aravind Srinivas said the median Perplexity employee now gets 7x more agent-hours a week from Teammates than in September, and one in five reach 40 or more.
key_facts.excerpt: The median Perplexity employee now gets 7x more agent-hours per week from teammates than in September. ... 1 in 5 are already at 40+ agent-hours a week, which is basically a full extra workweek.

key_facts.fact: Meta rolled out real-time voice conversations and expressive animated avatars in the Muse app in the US, announced on Nov. 5 by CEO Mark Zuckerberg.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta now lets you have voice conversations with your Muse AI agent in real time, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced today. ... Muse's voice mode and expressive avatars are rolling out now in the US for the app, Meta says.

key_facts.fact: Meta says the features are coming soon to its AI glasses and will also be available on its forthcoming Muse Charm gadget, due to ship this year.
key_facts.excerpt: They're coming "soon" for Meta's AI glasses and will also be available for its forthcoming Muse Charm gadget, which is supposed to ship this year.
